key_insight: CO-GRAFT shows that RL gains in search agents depend on role interactions and pre-RL capabilities, with query generation contributing no more than 15% of the total gain.
engineering_relevance: Role-level attribution can guide whether to prioritize reasoning, search decisions, or answer extraction rather than assuming better queries drive RL improvements.
method: Combine RL-trained and pre-RL policies in one closed-loop trajectory with live retrieval.
Evaluate all 16 assignments across reasoning, search-or-answer decisions, query generation, and answer extraction without retraining.
Use Shapley values to allocate gains and Möbius terms to measure role interactions.
evidence_signal: Evaluations of Search-R1 agents on NQ and HotpotQA span Qwen2.5 and Llama-3.2 models, two sizes, base and instruction-tuned initializations, and GRPO/PPO training, with RL gains reaching 32 exact-match points.
watch_item: Attributions depend on checkpoint capabilities and fixed task-level search budgets, so role rankings should not be assumed to generalize across deployments.
paper_title: CO-GRAFT: Attributing Reinforcement Learning Gains in Search Agents via Role-Level Policy Grafting
